notes: Translation-consistency glossary for assets/zh. Contains two blocks: the 18 division display names (keys 'division:<name>') and the content vocabulary. Every content entry was verified to occur in the English corpus (assets/en, 279 files) by scripts/term-count.mjs before being admitted; terms the corpus does not use were dropped rather than invented. MATCHING RULES: (1) keys are lowercase; look up case-insensitively and singular/plural-insensitively (agent/agents, workflow/workflows, metric/metrics all map to one headword), and treat '-' and '/' as equivalent to a space (post-mortem == postmortem, CI/CD == CI CD). (2) A key that is an extension of a longer key is matched as a whole phrase, so 'workflow process' wins over 'workflow'. (3) The value is the single approved rendering; a translator must not introduce a second synonym for the same key. (4) Values are Simplified Chinese and must be usable verbatim inside a sentence. (5) Proper nouns that are conventionally kept in Latin script in Chinese technical writing (API, CI/CD, Kubernetes, HIPAA, KPI, OKR, ROI, SEO, SLA, SLO, NPS, CSAT, MTTR, CRM, ETL, P&L, A/B testing) stay in Latin script deliberately; that is not residue. (6) True word-by-word synonyms are listed as separate keys only when the corpus uses both forms distinctly (e.g. 'post-mortem' vs 'retrospective'). (7) Keys prefixed 'division:' are the 18 division display names from upstream divisions.json and are used for navigation labels, not for prose consistency checks, so they are excluded from the glossary-consistency gate. Checks apply entry-by-entry: a key is only enforced in a file whose English source actually contains that key. (8) DELIBERATELY ABSENT - do not re-add: everyday English words whose domain rendering would be forced onto an ordinary sense. 'requirement' was removed because the upstream template phrase 'Default requirement:' occurs in 95 files and reads naturally as 默认要求, not 默认需求. 'patient' was removed because the adjective sense (patient but strict) was being forced into 患者. 'segmentation' was removed because the computer-vision sense (person segmentation) was being forced into the marketing term 分群. 'deal', 'acceptance' and the bare 'academic' were removed for the same reason: a generic word whose approved rendering only fits one domain. The specific multi-word forms ('acceptance criteria') stay.
